title: GPS only works because of Einstein's relativity
description: GPS satellite clocks drift from Earth time because of speed and gravity. Without a fix, errors would grow by kilometers every day.

scenes.say: GPS only works because of Einstein. Without relativity fixes, your phone's map would drift off by kilometers within a day.

steps: Satellite sends its time and position
Your phone times the signal delay
Four satellites pin down your spot
scenes.say: Here's the idea. Each GPS satellite broadcasts the exact time. Your receiver measures how late the signal arrives, and multiplies by the speed of light to get distance. With four satellites in view, it can work out where you are.
But light covers about thirty centimeters in one nanosecond. So the satellite clocks must be incredibly accurate, or your position goes wrong.

And relativity messes with them. Moving fast makes satellite clocks tick slower. Weaker gravity makes them tick faster. Gravity wins by about thirty-eight microseconds a day, which would add up to roughly eleven kilometers, or seven miles, of error.
So engineers tune the satellite clocks slightly slow before launch. Once in orbit, they tick in step with Earth. Follow for more science behind your tech.
